title: Scope the merge's docs/knowledge auto-commit to the merging feature, the way docs/history already is
action: bee worktree merge auto-commits main's dirty bookkeeping before merging, so the dirty-main guard cannot deadlock against the worktree-first rule. main_bookkeeping_roots (packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/worktree/merge.rs:184-190) returns .bee, docs/decisions, docs/knowledge as BLANKET roots and docs/history/<feature> as a feature-SCOPED one. The asymmetry is deliberate for history — tests.rs:1804-1833 (another_features_docs_history_dirt_still_refuses_and_is_named) already proves a peer feature's docs/history is left alone and still refuses. The intent to scope exists; it was never carried to docs/knowledge. REAL INCIDENT, 2026-08-18: merging uat-stop-placement produced bookkeeping commit 7429dfda which swallowed 21 insertions of a SIBLING session's spec sync to docs/knowledge/areas/workflow-state/gates.md, work belonging to feature start-feature-reservation-scope. Nothing was lost; the authorship and the feature attribution were both wrong. A peer session found it, no test did. docs/knowledge/ is the ONE root in that list holding AUTHORED prose — .bee is the machine-written control plane and docs/decisions is its rendered index, so sweeping those is bookkeeping, while sweeping authored capture is taking someone else's work. FIX: scope docs/knowledge the way docs/history already is, using data bee already keeps. feature_touched_files(root, feature) at packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/drivers/close.rs:1388 is ALREADY pub(crate) and already returns the merging feature's own capped cells' files_changed — close.rs's own doc-deferral scan set uses it exactly this way, so this is an established read, not a new concept. Call it, filter its result to paths under docs/knowledge/, and pass those exact paths in place of the blanket docs/knowledge root. Everything under docs/knowledge/ that this feature's cells did NOT record stays uncommitted, and the EXISTING dirty-main refusal names it — that path is already built and already tested, and the instruction it gives a sibling (commit your own capture) is the honest one. Keep .bee and docs/decisions blanket: they are machine-written and shared, and narrowing them would trade a real deadlock for an attribution nicety. Keep the commit subject honest — if it still names docs/knowledge it should read as the feature's own, not the whole tree; adjust the string at phases.rs:217-222 to match what is actually swept, and keep the feature-less arm working. Do NOT change the dirty-main refusal's shape or message contract, the worktree_merge_commit_bookkeeping opt-out (merge.rs:201-206), or bee close's own .bee-only bookkeeping commit. Do NOT edit packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/drivers/close.rs — it is reserved by another session's cell ddb-1; feature_touched_files is CALLED, never changed. TESTS: docs_knowledge_dirt_is_auto_committed_alongside_bee (tests.rs:1758-1795) is the one whose expectation changes — rewrite it so this feature's OWN recorded knowledge dirt is swept, and add its mirror proving a SIBLING feature's docs/knowledge dirt is NOT swept and still refuses while naming the file, modelled line-for-line on another_features_docs_history_dirt_still_refuses_and_is_named (tests.rs:1804-1833). Also cover: a knowledge file dirty but recorded by no cell of this feature stays uncommitted; and the feature-less merge arm (main_bookkeeping_roots(None)) still behaves. Every other test in tests.rs:1622-1893 must still pass unchanged.
done_when: A merge sweeps only the docs/knowledge paths the merging feature's own capped cells recorded; a sibling feature's docs/knowledge dirt is left uncommitted and named by the existing dirty-main refusal; .bee and docs/decisions are still swept blanket; the opt-out, the refusal contract, and bee close's own bookkeeping commit are unchanged; the commit subject describes what is actually swept; close.rs is untouched; and the worktree suite is green.
notes: Third of three defects the owner queued. Files are disjoint from the two cells other sessions hold (drivers/close.rs, drivers/tests.rs, .gitignore, herding/*).
